title: Compensability and Payer Terms for the Workers' Compensation Referral
content:
# Compensability and payer terms

The North Carolina Industrial Commission forms filed by the carrier decide who pays for treatment under a Workers' Compensation Referral. This table sets, per program, whether the injured worker is protected from billing on a compensable claim, whether treatment may start while compensability is still pending and for how many visits, how long the carrier may still deny after a Form 63, and whether treatment under a denied claim is rebilled to the worker's health insurance and within what period.

| Program | Worker never billed on a compensable claim | Treat while compensability pending | Visits while pending | Form 63 contest period (calendar days) | Denied claim rebilled to health insurance | Health insurance rebill within (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Employer Direct Early Intervention | Yes | No | 0 | 0 | No | 0 |
| Workers' Comp Outpatient Therapy | Yes | Yes | 3 | 90 | Yes | 60 |
| Workers' Comp Post-Surgical Therapy | Yes | No | 0 | 90 | Yes | 60 |
| Work Conditioning Program | Yes | No | 0 | 90 | Yes | 60 |
| Work Hardening Program | Yes | No | 0 | 90 | Yes | 60 |
| Functional Capacity Evaluation | Yes | No | 0 | 90 | Yes | 60 |

## Definitions

- **Worker never billed on a compensable claim** — whether the injured worker may never be billed for treatment of an accepted or without-prejudice claim.
- **Treat while compensability pending** — whether treatment may start while compensability is still pending; this does not apply to programs priced under an employer contract.
- **Visits while pending** — the visits rendered while compensability is pending before treatment pauses; 0 where treatment does not start while pending.
- **Form 63 contest period** — the calendar days after a Form 63 (payment without prejudice) within which the carrier may still deny the claim; 0 where not applicable.
- **Denied claim rebilled to health insurance** — whether treatment under a denied claim is rebilled to the worker's health insurance.
- **Health insurance rebill within** — the calendar days after a claim denial within which treatment is rebilled to the worker's health insurance; 0 where not applicable.

## Comparisons

- Every program protects the worker from billing on a compensable claim.
- Workers' Comp Outpatient Therapy is the only program that treats while compensability is pending, for up to 3 visits; all others show 0.
- The five carrier-billed programs share a 90-day Form 63 contest period and rebill a denied claim to health insurance within 60 days; Employer Direct Early Intervention shows 0 for both and does not rebill.
